title: He Told Her All His Heart
reflectionText: It was not the cords or the ropes that overcame him. It was words, pressed on him day after day, until his soul was troubled to death. Then he woke believing he would shake himself free as at other times, not knowing that Yahweh had departed. What is it that wears a strength down — not all at once, but a little every day, until it is gone?
editorialNotes: Text-First Story Factory 2.0 Batch A (journey backlog G4, approved 2026-07-22). Judges 16:4-22, absent both lanes. Fills the Samson-arc middle between existing 1142 (Judges 13, birth) and 1193 (Judges 16:23-31, death); VOICE_ARCHER shared with 1193 is a deliberate arc-continuity choice mirroring the 1564/1336 precedent. Boundary: ends at v22 (the hair beginning to grow again — the source's own seam into 1193) with no temple or death material and no forward-looking narration. SHORT + FULL (WEB 398w / 598w; KJV 440w / 515w). LONG omitted: the 19-verse source (~619 WEB words) has its honest ceiling inside the FULL band (same honest-ceiling finding as 1564 / 1 Samuel 24, ADR-030/031). Delilah's motive stated as the lords' silver only; Samson's torment carried by the source's own words ('his soul was troubled to death'); the cry 'The Philistines be upon thee, Samson!' kept from the source. SHORT compresses the three false answers into one movement. CODEX-AUDIT CORRECTION 2026-07-23 (Finding 3, accepted as full-source paraphrase): the KJV FULL was re-authored from a verse-tracking paraphrase (was run 41 / 89.2% coverage) into an independently-composed retelling that clusters the three tests into a patterned reported-speech movement and breaks the source clause sequence (now run 9 / 20.4% coverage, 515w); the Nazarite confession and 'he wist not that the Lord was departed' are kept as essential lines. Per Finding 7, the figure-registry framing line was corrected from 'three times the ambush waited' to 'twice the hidden men waited in vain' — Judges 16 states men lying in wait only for the first two tests (16:9, 16:12); the KJV FULL likewise names the ambush only in rounds one and two. WEB short/full and KJV short unchanged.
